comparator.name: International Business
comparator.sourceNotes: The first two years each contain 60 EC of required courses. Year three includes a 30 EC choice among study abroad, a selective internship and faculty minors. The final 30 EC includes a required 10 EC thesis.
components: Study abroad, International Business internship or approved faculty minor
Research Design and Data Analytics for IB

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: International strategy, markets, trade and cross-border business operations
Marketing, supply chains and multinational operations
Sustainable multinational business, corporate responsibility and ethics
Finance, accounting, economics and investment for international business
Business research, statistics, qualitative methods and analytics
Innovation and digital transformation in multinational firms
Global political economy, governance and international business law
adjacent: Business analytics, AI and digital transformation
International finance, trade and political economy
questions: How should multinational firms make strategic decisions across markets, cultures and stakeholder environments?
How do data, innovation and emerging technologies reshape international business?
How do finance, trade and political economy shape cross-border investment and competition?

trace: Develops academic writing, source evaluation, collaboration and reflection on professional development.
Uses financial statements, costing and performance measures to evaluate firms and their decisions.
Examines how AI changes business processes, market structure, labour and organisational responsibilities.
Applies trade, contract and dispute rules to cross-border transactions and digital commerce.
Studies securities valuation, interest-rate risk, financial institutions and banking regulation.
Introduces production costs, competition, markets and the economic environment of firms.
Studies exchange rates and open-economy macroeconomic policy to assess conditions affecting cross-border business.
Uses microeconomic models to examine market power, strategic behaviour and choices under uncertainty.
Examines how taxation, redistribution and responses to market failure change economic incentives.
Uses regression, instrumental variables and statistical testing to assess causal and predictive claims in economic data.
Uses experiments to study how framing, heuristics and biases affect economic decisions.
Tests product concepts and prototypes against consumer needs, production costs and environmental impacts.
Uses consumer research and customer journeys to develop marketing and engagement strategies.
Uses cases to develop a strategy for organisational change, digital value and responsible implementation.
Uses primary market research and analysis to evaluate customer preferences and support business decisions.
Examines trade, investment, market entry and the institutions shaping multinational strategy.
Uses venture planning and customer validation to study business models, operations and competitive positioning.
Uses research design, measurement, sampling and statistical inference to investigate management questions.
Examines motivation, self-regulation and group dynamics in the practice of leadership.
Examines leadership communication, ethics and the influence of culture on organisational relationships.
Uses research on emotions, work pressure and inclusion to examine decisions and behaviour within teams.
Examines motivation, teams, organisational culture and conflict through cases and research synthesis.
Practises negotiation and strategic decision-making across organisational and cultural settings.
Examines fairness, privacy and accountability in AI applications and their organisational effects.
Uses relational database design and SQL to organise and retrieve business data.
Implements and evaluates data structures and algorithms for processing data and comparing performance.
Cleans, integrates and visualises data to support evidence-based analysis.
Uses regression, classification and validation to compare predictive models on real data.
Trains neural networks and evaluates models for prediction, image and text tasks relevant to digital services.
Develops Python programming, testing and debugging for automation and data analysis.
Develops calculus, optimisation and matrix foundations for quantitative modelling.
Uses linear transformations and matrix decompositions to model and analyse multidimensional data.
Uses probability distributions, estimation and inference to reason about data and uncertainty.
Examines EU institutions, lobbying and legislative decisions that shape cross-border market rules.
Uses a comparative case and policy memos to analyse how national and international institutions make policy.
Uses interviews, focus groups, documentary evidence and coding to investigate organisational and social practices.

alternatives.label: International business and management
alternatives.concept: Combines international strategy and business law with marketing, management, accounting and finance. Courses in research, leadership and product design help students analyse decisions about organisations and markets.
alternatives.labelReason: Business, economics and research foundations precede finance, marketing, global business law and advanced organisation work.
progression: Business, economics and research foundations precede finance, marketing, global business law and advanced organisation work.
traceOverrides: Examines how AI changes business processes, market structure, labour and organisational responsibilities.
Studies securities valuation, interest-rate risk, financial institutions and banking regulation.
Studies exchange rates and open-economy macroeconomic policy to assess conditions affecting cross-border business.
Uses cases to develop a strategy for organisational change, digital value and responsible implementation.
Cleans, integrates and visualises data to support evidence-based analysis.
Uses regression, classification and validation to compare predictive models on real data.

alternatives.label: Business, AI and digital transformation
alternatives.concept: Studies how organisations use data and AI to change their operations and strategy. Programming, machine learning and AI ethics complement work in digital business, marketing and organisational behaviour.
alternatives.labelReason: Programming, mathematics and research foundations support machine learning and neural networks. Business foundations support digital strategy and international governance.
alternatives.distinctness: Programming, data infrastructure, machine learning and digital strategy shape the selection.
progression: Programming, mathematics and research foundations support machine learning and neural networks. Business foundations support digital strategy and international governance.

alternatives.label: International finance, trade and economic policy
alternatives.concept: Studies how firms and institutions respond to international markets, financial risks and trade policy. It combines accounting, banking and econometrics with business law and analysis of economic policy.
alternatives.labelReason: Economics, accounting and research foundations support international macroeconomics, finance and econometrics. Law and politics support policy analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: Banking, econometrics, international trade and economic institutions shape the selection.
progression: Economics, accounting and research foundations support international macroeconomics, finance and econometrics. Law and politics support policy analysis.

candidates.label: International finance, trade and economic policy

selection.assessment: The broad option centres international business, management and organisations. The second concentrates on digital business and analytics, and the third on finance, trade and economic policy. All three are distinct and reach the maximum.

blocks: Both teach how financial transactions are recorded and how to interpret financial statements.
Both use legal rules and cases to examine cross-border business.
Both study valuation, risk and financial markets. UCR also examines banking and financial regulation.
Both develop marketing strategy and examine customers. Groningen focuses on differences across international markets.
Both examine how firms respond to digital change and use cases to develop strategies. Groningen focuses on international firms.
Both examine how multinational firms choose markets and organise cross-border operations.
Both develop research design, measurement and analysis for business questions.
Groningen requires dedicated study of global supply chains.
UCR studies business foundations and cross-border strategy in separate courses. Groningen introduces multinational firms as a field.
UCR studies investment and market entry in global business. Groningen gives firm location and foreign direct investment dedicated attention.
UCR addresses responsible business and AI ethics in separate courses. Groningen teaches ethics across international business settings.
Groningen requires a dedicated history of global business.
Groningen requires a systematic comparison of national business and investment environments.
UCR studies product design and digital strategy. Groningen examines innovation management across multinational organisations.
Both introduce production, costs and market competition. Groningen applies microeconomics to business decisions.
Both examine exchange rates and macroeconomic conditions across borders. Groningen also gives dedicated attention to trade barriers and competition.
Both use regression to address questions about cause and effect. Groningen also teaches causal diagrams and panel data methods.
UCR accounting includes cost and sustainability topics and is aligned to financial accounting. Groningen requires separate management accounting.
UCR studies macroeconomics, institutions and public policy across separate courses. Groningen studies global political economy as a field.
Groningen studies financial management of multinational firms. UCR financial markets and valuation are aligned to Finance and Investment for IB.
Both examine motivation, individual differences and behaviour in teams.
Both examine how cultural differences affect interactions at work. UCR applies these ideas to negotiation.
UCR studies organisational behaviour and leadership. Groningen gives organisational structure dedicated attention.
Groningen integrates operations, finance and other business functions in the management of international organisations.
Both introduce probability, estimation and inference. Groningen applies them to international business.
Both teach qualitative research design and interpretation. Groningen applies these methods to business questions.
UCR covers data, research and econometrics in several courses. Groningen links advanced business research design and analytics in one course.
Both develop academic and professional skills through reflection and practice.
Students choose 30 EC of approved study abroad, internship or a faculty minor.
Groningen requires a thesis. UCR independent research is optional.

notes.text: UCR offers related study in international business, finance, management and analytics. Groningen requires dedicated work in global supply chains, firm location, international financial management and a thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: International Business at the University of Groningen studies how firms operate across countries and cultures. Students study strategy, finance, marketing and operations, then complete an approved choice semester and a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines international business and management. The other options give more attention to digital transformation and AI, or to finance, trade and economic policy.

componentNotes.y3-choice: Students complete 30 EC through approved study abroad, a selective internship or an approved faculty minor.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: The thesis requires the complete first year, at least 60 EC of higher-year International Business courses and an approved study programme.
